normalization_notes: ENERGY STAR Enterprise Server certification IDs are immutable issuer identities, not installed deployments.
All 100 HPE entries retain exact issuer models and platform socket attributes; repeated model names remain separate by certification ID.
Ninety-nine HPE entries retain low-end, typical/single and high-end SERT configurations; HPE ProLiant Compute DL110 Gen12 retains only typical/single and no absent tier is synthesized.
HPE 1P/2P/4P model text is not substituted for platform socket capacity or tested installed-processor population.
PSU nameplates, SERT idle watts, workload efficiency scores and total-server power scores are not normalized as rated server or rack input.
Maximum supported memory is not treated as installed memory.
All 123 Dell entries retain exact issuer models and platform socket attributes; repeated model names remain separate by certification ID.
One hundred twenty Dell entries retain low-end, typical/single and high-end SERT configurations; E127S and two E128S entries retain only typical/single and no absent tier is synthesized.
Dell -1P configuration labels are not substituted for two-socket platform capacity or tested installed-processor population.
All 49 Super Micro entries retain three reported SERT observation tiers; 35 rows have no tier-specific configuration IDs and no identifier is inferred.
Super Micro Product Processor Socket Count values of Greater than 4 remain text observations with normalized processor_socket_count null.
Supermicro and Super Micro Computer, Inc. brand labels remain source observations under the canonical Supermicro manufacturer identity.
All 45 Lenovo entries retain low-end, typical/single and high-end SERT observations; missing tier-specific configuration IDs remain absent rather than being synthesized.
Lenovo platform socket attributes remain exact source observations and are not replaced by tested installed-processor counts.
All 14 ASUSTeK entries retain three SERT tiers, all three configuration IDs and exact one- or two-socket platform attributes.
All nine H3C entries retain three SERT tiers; four G7 rows omit the low-end configuration ID and no identifier is inferred.
ASUSTeK SERT 2.0.7/2.0.8 and H3C SERT 2.0.6/2.0.8 revisions remain exact issuer observations.
All nine IBM entries retain exact issuer SERT observations; Power S1014 has no reported high-end tier, and the printed combined 2.0.4; 2.0.6 version value remains exact.
All eight Aivres partner entries retain KAYTUS as the source brand and only the reported typical/single tier; Aivres partner identity is not discarded or promoted to a deployment.
All three Altos and the one Ace Computers entry retain only typical/single SERT observations; absent low-end/high-end tiers and configuration IDs remain absent.
All six ZTE and three Oracle entries retain their reported three-tier observations. ZTE certification 4654814 does not resolve its R5300 G5/R5300 G6 configuration-label mismatch.
All 476 rows across all 17 ENERGY STAR Enterprise Servers partner partitions in the 2026-11-04 dataset snapshot are now processed.
Campus aggregates remain excluded from capacity sums under all viewer filters.
NTT, PeeringDB, PDG, Socomec, Airedale, Riello and Kohler/Rehlko reuse holds remain in force; no held facts or bytes were imported.
